What's changed

This page lists the changes to mta-mcp that a reader would notice: new tools, new data, changes to the website, and corrections when the server gave a wrong answer. Newest first. Routine data refreshes are not listed.

  • History begins: 2026-09-17, the first version. Corrections made before this date may be missing.
  • Data refresh: Service alerts and elevator and escalator outages come from MTA's live feeds each time a tool is called. Station names, each station's accessibility status and MTA's elevator inventory are snapshots kept in the repository and refreshed by hand when needed.

mta-mcp is not published to npm. You run it from your own copy of the repository, so a change reaches you when you update that copy and rebuild it. To report a bug in this server or ask for a new feature, open an issue on GitHub.

Ask where the data comes from

Not released yet

Tags: MCP

A new tool lets your AI assistant answer "where does this come from?" for any answer from this server. It names the source behind each kind of data: MTA's live feeds for service alerts and elevator outages, and MTA's station list, station accessibility status and elevator inventory, which this server keeps as dated copies. For each, it says whether the figures are MTA's own record or have been changed by BetaNYC, how current they are on your copy, where to check a figure at MTA, and where to report a mistake. It also gives BetaNYC's address for questions about the data, lab@beta.nyc.

MCP version: mta-mcp 0.3.0

Answers warn when the station and elevator data are old

October 12, 2026

Tags: MCP, Data

Station names, accessibility status and the elevator inventory come from copies of MTA's data kept in the repository, and nothing updates them on its own. Every answer that uses one now gives the date it was pulled, and warns when the station accessibility or elevator copy is more than 30 days old or the station list more than 90 days old.

MCP version: mta-mcp as built from the main branch from October 12, 2026 on. The version number was still 0.1.0; the release notes list this under 0.2.0.

More detail: Pull request · Keep your data current

Link to this change: Answers warn when the station and elevator data are old

Station accessibility status, and MTA's routes around broken elevators

September 23, 2026

Tags: MCP, Data

Every station the server looks up now says whether MTA lists it as fully accessible, partly accessible or not accessible. When you ask about one station, each elevator or escalator outage there carries MTA's own alternate route, and outages are placed at the station by MTA's equipment number first, with names only as a fallback. A route check can also include the station's elevator outages that day.

MCP version: mta-mcp as built from the main branch from September 23, 2026 on. The version number was still 0.1.0; the release notes list this under 0.2.0.

Some elevator outages were missed or shown at the wrong station

September 23, 2026

Tags: MCP, Correction

From September 17 to September 23, 2026, MTA's elevator feed spelled some stations differently from the station list, and the server did not match them. Searches for Bedford Park Blvd and 42 St-Port Authority returned no outages when there were some. Matching by name also put some outages at a different station with a similar name: against the saved feeds, 13 such pairings were wrong. The fixes on September 23 match the different spellings and place outages by MTA's equipment number first.

If you used the old numbers: If you checked elevators or escalators at a station during that week, for example to tell people which station to use, check the station again with the current version. Elevator status changes often, so an answer from that week is out of date in any case.

MCP version: mta-mcp as built from the main branch from September 23, 2026 on. The version number was still 0.1.0; the release notes list this under 0.2.0.

More detail: The first fix · The second fix · Elevators, escalators and accessibility

Link to this change: Some elevator outages were missed or shown at the wrong station

Service alerts that gave no dates were left out of every date

September 23, 2026

Tags: MCP, Correction

From September 17 to September 23, 2026, a service alert that gave no dates was counted as active on no date at all, so a route check could miss it. The GTFS-realtime reference says such an alert is active all the time, and since September 23 the server counts it on every date.

If you used the old numbers: If you checked a route for a date during that week and the answer said it was not disrupted, check it again with the current version. The record does not show whether MTA's feed carried an alert with no dates that week.

MCP version: mta-mcp as built from the main branch from September 23, 2026 on. The version number was still 0.1.0; the release notes list this under 0.2.0.

More detail: The fix

The elevator and escalator tool can now list outages for a given date or a given subway line, and says what to try next when a search finds nothing. A skill for Claude Code runs the same tools from the command line, with no MCP server. Every tool now returns shorter answers.

First version, with four tools for subway alerts, elevators and stations

September 17, 2026

Tags: MCP

The first version went up on GitHub. Its four tools check whether a subway line is disrupted on a date at a station, list the service alerts for a date, find a station by name, and list elevator and escalator outages. It is not on npm, because MTA's data terms rule out a published package.
